[[File:Norfolk Marriott Waterside.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Norfolk Marriott Waterside, January 2016.]]
'''1997 Decipher World Championship''' was the second Star Wars CCG World Championship, played 6–7 December 1997 at the Norfolk Marriott Waterside Hotel in Norfolk, Virginia, Decipher's hometown.<ref name="dec-index">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/index.html 1997 World Championship], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980223180018/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dec-overview">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/overview.html 1997 World Championship overview], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981203142434/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/overview.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dec-report1">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/report1.html Star Wars Finalists Arrive in Norfolk], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980224024525/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/report1.html Internet Archive]</ref> Players arrived Friday 5 December. Decipher billed the weekend 5–7 December 1997.<ref name="dec-index" /><ref name="dec-report1" /> [[Philipp Jacobs]] (Germany) defeated [[Michael Riboulet]] (United Kingdom) in the final. It was the first Worlds final for either country.<ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]]</ref><ref name="dec-score">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/scoreboard.html Championship scoreboard], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990210171544/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/scoreboard.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher invited 53 champions. [[Tracey Gamble]], the [[1997 DragonCon Open]] champion, was unable to attend. 52 players competed Saturday.<ref name="dec-index" /><ref name="dec-finalists">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/finalists.html 1997 World Championship finalists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980223180125/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/finalists.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dec-sat">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/satsummary.html Saturday's Event Summary], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980224024206/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/satsummary.html Internet Archive]</ref> [[Cloud City Limited|Cloud City]] had just hit the shelves.<ref name="trando" /> Jacobs's prize was a 10-day trip from Washington to Las Vegas and Los Angeles. Decipher billed a coast-to-coast United States prizetrip.<ref name="jacobs">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050405/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/iv6.htm Philipp Jacobs interview], [[Trandosite]] (24 August 2000)</ref><ref name="dec-index" />

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Cloud City]]
* '''Site:''' Norfolk Marriott Waterside Hotel, Norfolk, Virginia<ref name="dec-report1" />
* '''Dates:''' 5–7 December 1997. Friday arrival and registration. Saturday and Sunday constructed play.<ref name="dec-index" /><ref name="dec-report1" />
* '''Field:''' 53 invited, 52 played<ref name="dec-index" /><ref name="dec-sat" />
* '''Swiss:''' 2 victory points for a win, plus Force differential<ref name="dec-sat" />
* '''Saturday:''' eight preliminary games, four rounds of two games each, cut to twelve<ref name="dec-report1" /><ref name="dec-finalists" />
* '''Sunday:''' two rounds of two games each among the twelve, then a two-game final<ref name="dec-report1" />

== Qualifiers ==

Fifty-one players qualified by winning 40 Regional qualifiers and 11 Open events. They were joined by two invitees: defending champion [[Raphael Asselin]], and Michel Safady of Brazil for the Outer Rim (players beyond the sanctioned regions).<ref name="dec97q">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/regionalsandopens.html 1997 Regionals and Open Events], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990503132332/http://search.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/regionalsandopens.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher named 53 champions who earned a seat by those Regionals and Opens, or by special invitation. Gamble was on that list and was unable to attend. 52 played Saturday.<ref name="dec-finalists" /><ref name="dec-sat" /> [[Eric Berger]] earned his trip by winning the Texas regional at Texas A&M University in College Station, 8–0.<ref name="ars">[https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ That one time I played in the Star Wars card game world championship], Eric Berger, Ars Technica (5 December 2015). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009010838/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Day 1 ==

[[Stuart Lauder]] of Brisbane, the Australian Open champion, arrived Wednesday evening after thirty hours of flight. Friday 5 December, champions registered at the Norfolk Marriott Waterside Hotel, toured Decipher's offices, and attended a 6–8 p.m. reception. Gold Leader [[Kendrick Summers]], Red Leader [[Allen Divers]], and Rebel Base Leader [[Tom Lischke]] held a Q&A on rulings and the World Finals Code of Conduct.<ref name="dec-report1" />

Saturday 6 December was eight rounds of preliminary play. Breakfast and deck building ran 7–8 a.m. Play ran 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.: four rounds of two games each, with lunch noon–1 p.m. The twelve semi-finalists advanced.<ref name="dec-report1" /><ref name="dec-finalists" /> [[Tom Braunlich]] counted 208 games in the first round. Light won 107. Dark won 101.<ref name="dec-lvd">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/lightvsdark.html Light vs. Dark Stats], Tom Braunlich, Decipher (7 December 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980224024100/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/lightvsdark.html Internet Archive]</ref>

[[Reiner Zetsche]] of Duisburg finished Saturday first at 14 (91), seven wins and one loss. [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] of Wuppertal was second at 14 (81), ten Force behind. Both were undefeated through six games and split their last two.<ref name="dec-sat" /><ref name="dec-semi">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/semifinalists.html The twelve semi-finalists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980224024312/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/semifinalists.html Internet Archive]</ref> [[Thaddeus Chenoweth]] of Colorado Springs sat third at 13 (70). [[Philipp Jacobs]] of Dortmund sat ninth at 10 (71). Defending champion [[Raphael Asselin]] sat twelfth at 10 (48). Three Force differential separated him from thirteenth, [[Erik Petersen]]. After four games Asselin led with 8 victory points. He then lost three, and won game 8 to make the twelve. Petersen lost game 8 by two Force to [[Enrique Pascual]].<ref name="dec-sat" /><ref name="dec-semi" />

Returning 1996 finalists [[Joe Alread]] and [[Paul Todd Feldman]] made the twelve.<ref name="dec-sat" /> [[Maarten Logghe]] won his first three, lost to Asselin by 16 in game 4, and finished 8 (+9). [[Stuart Jones]] lost his first four, then won his last four by an average of 17 Force, and finished 21st.<ref name="dec-sat" /> [[Eric Berger]] later wrote that he won one game of six and finished near the bottom of a field he remembered as about 64 players.<ref name="ars" />

Alread used a Hoth Clouds deck for both sides on day one. [[Jerry Darcy]] called the decks "somewhat counter to the general Star Wars storyline."<ref name="trando" /> Saturday night the Day 2 field built new decks. Jacobs said he had barely made the second day.<ref name="jacobs" />

== Day 2 ==

The twelve returned Sunday 7 December. Two rounds of two games each ran 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. The top two then played a two-game final from 1:30 to 3:30 p.m.<ref name="dec-report1" />

Asselin opened Dark against Palmer Light and lost 0 (−2).<ref name="dec-sun">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/gameresults2.html Sunday semi-final results], Decipher (7 December 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990427191534/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/gameresults2.html Internet Archive]</ref> Asselin later said he lost that game on a [[DS-61-4]] passenger / [[Devastator]] ruling, and called himself a "scrub at the second day."<ref name="asselin">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv11.htm Raphael Asselin interview], Trandosite (21 September 2000)</ref> Jacobs's third game was Dark against Riboulet Light.<ref name="dec-sun" /> Jacobs later said Riboulet's Light in the final was a Dagobah deck he had beaten the previous round.<ref name="jacobs" /> After four games Jacobs led at 7 (51). Riboulet sat second at 6 (54). Feldman sat third at 6 (51). Palmer sat fourth at 6 (28).<ref name="dec-sun" /> Feldman later called 1997 his best Worlds showing.<ref name="feldman-pds2">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I SWCCG PDS2: DRTORCH Worlds Finalist 1996, 1997, 1999, 2000 Interview], BillBisco2 (29 May 2025). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261014143045/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Championship match ===

In game one Jacobs played Dark. Starting locations were [[Hoth: Defensive Perimeter (3rd Marker)]] and the [[Dagobah]] system. Jacobs deployed [[Darth Vader]], walkers, and [[Imperial Decree]]. Riboulet trained at Dagobah with [[Clouds]]. Jacobs won by 23 Force.<ref name="dec-pbp">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/eventreports.html Championship play by play], Sandy Wible / Kendrick Summers / Tom Lischke, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980223111440/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/eventreports.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dec-score" />

In game two Riboulet played Dark. Starting locations were [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]] and [[Hoth: Ice Plains]]. Riboulet played [[Scanning Crew]] and manipulator effects. The 15-minute time limit was called. Riboulet won by 11 Force.<ref name="dec-pbp" /><ref name="dec-score" />

The combined score was Jacobs 2 (+12), Riboulet 2 (−12). Jacobs was champion.<ref name="dec-score" /> Alread called Riboulet's manipulator "a truly great deck....that I had never seen before." Trandosite treats 1997 as the birthplace of that strategy.<ref name="trando" />

=== First Anthology sealed ===

While the twelve played, the other 40 played a [[First Anthology]] sealed tournament. Each received a First Anthology set signed by Decipher's product development team. Decipher wrote there were only fifty-two sets like it. [[Kyle Kessenich]] of California defeated [[Colin McCann]] of Ontario in the final. Kessenich's prize was a Japanese Premiere complete set.<ref name="dec-sealed">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/sealedsummary.html Report 10], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980223172645/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/sealedsummary.html Internet Archive]</ref>
